# Motion Studio

The studio lives at `motion-studio/` in the `ahmadscb/ahmad` repository (VPS: wherever it is cloned). Design rules come from the **bang-motion** plugin skill. Read its `SKILL.md` (anti-PPT laws, style brief, camera) and, for characters, `references/kartun-panggung.md`. This skill adds production: rendering, sound, QC and limits.

## Workflow (do all of it; never stop at a storyboard)

1. Write `projects/<name>/brief.json` (schema `workflow/brief.template.json`):
   - format, type, **style** (one of the six in `lib/styles.js`), message;
   - script/dialogue, cast (from the 10 library characters), sets;
   - a shot-by-shot storyboard with times, sfx and music.
2. Scaffold with `bin/bm-new <name> --dur <s> --template cartoon` (character stories) or `--template reel` (type and graphics).
   Then build `index.html` from the **asset library** (`workflow/LIBRARY.md`):
   - `BM.CH` characters, expressions, poses and actions;
   - `BM.ENV` sets and `BM.PROP` props;
   - `BM.CAM` moves and `BM.TR` transitions;
   - `BM.say` / `BM.CAP` for subtitles and bubbles;
   - `BM.STYLE` style packs;
   - `BM.sfx` / `BM.music` for sound.
   
   Draw new things only when the library lacks them. 3D: `lib/product3d.js` (see `projects/aether-ad`).
3. **Dialogue:** write `dialogue.json` and run `python3 tools/voice.py projects/<name>/dialogue.json projects/<name>/voice`.
   - It's a free local voice per character, with lip-sync visemes.
   - Time the shots from `voice/dialog.json`.
4. Run `node tools/snap.mjs projects/<name> /tmp/check <times…>` and **look at `sheet.jpg`** (Read the image). Fix:
   - clipped or overlapping text;
   - off-model characters;
   - empty or slide-like frames;
   - props hidden behind other layers.
   
   Repeat until clean.
5. Run `bin/bm-render projects/<name> --voice projects/<name>/voice/dialog.wav` (omit `--voice` if there's no dialogue; `--blur 2` adds motion blur).
6. Inspect frames taken **from the MP4** (`ffmpeg -i out/<name>.mp4 -vf fps=1/1.5,scale=216:-1,tile=10x2 -frames:v 1 sheet.jpg`) and read `out/qc.txt`. Repair and re-render until clean.
7. Report the MP4, `out/render-metrics.json` (time, peak RAM, peak CPU), and what was checked.

## Guardrails

- Zero paid APIs by default. ElevenLabs needs `--allow-paid`, plus `allow_paid` in the brief, plus an environment key. Never print or store keys.
- Never publish. Renders run under `bin/bm-safe` (memory cap, CPU cores, low priority). Don't touch other services.
- Determinism: no `Math.random`, no clocks, no network during render (fonts, GSAP and three.js are vendored).
- Never put a `//` comment in the middle of a line of code. It disables the rest of the line.

## References

- **Sarcastic Grotesque** (face-first reaction-meme comedy, separate cast of 10 with 33 deforming expressions): `workflow/GROTESQUE.md`, `templates/grotesque`; agent: `bin/bm-agent "<brief>" --style grotesque --run`.
- **Library API:** `workflow/LIBRARY.md`. Visual catalog: `library/catalog`. Six-style showcase: `library/styles`.
- **Worked examples:** `templates/cartoon` (library demo with voice), `projects/crypto-crash` (2D comedy), `projects/aether-ad` (3D product ad).
- **Sound:** `tools/sound.py` (53 effects, 12 music styles, two-pass −14 LUFS).
- **Voice:** `tools/voice.py` (local Piper/LibriTTS-R, CC BY 4.0) and `tools/lipsync.py` (audio to visemes).
# Motion Studio pipeline: prompt to MP4

Each stage has one owner (the agent or a script) and one artefact, so another agent (Hermes, a scheduler, a human) can take over at any boundary.

| # | Stage | Owner | Artefact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Creative brief** | agent | `projects/<name>/brief.json` (schema: `workflow/brief.template.json`) |
| 2 | **Style brief + storyboard** | agent, following the Bang Motion `SKILL.md` | `brief.json` → `style_brief`, `storyboard[]` (t0/t1, shot, camera, text, sfx, music) |
| 3 | **Scaffold** | `bin/bm-new <name> --dur N --template cartoon\|reel` | `projects/<name>/index.html` (bm-core + library, local GSAP/fonts) |
| 4 | **Visual assets** | agent | asset library first (`workflow/LIBRARY.md`: 10 characters, 9 sets, 17 props, 6 styles); new SVG only when missing; 3D via `lib/product3d.js` |
| 5 | **Animation** | agent | the GSAP timeline: stages + cameras, `BM.sfx()` and `BM.music()` cues next to the visual they belong to |
| 6 | **Dialogue / narration** (optional) | `tools/voice.py dialogue.json voice/` (characters, local) or `tools/narration.py` | `dialog.wav` + `dialog.json` (line timings + lip-sync visemes). ElevenLabs only with `--allow-paid` |
| 7 | **Key-frame QC** | `node tools/snap.mjs projects/<name> out/check t1 t2 …` | `sheet.jpg`. The agent **looks** at it: clipped or overlapping text, off-model character, slide feel, empty frames |
| 8 | **Render** | `bin/bm-render projects/<name> [--voice vo.wav] [--blur 2]` | `out/<name>.mp4`, `render-metrics.json` (resource-limited by `bin/bm-safe`) |
| 9 | **Video QC** | `tools/qc.sh` (run by bm-render) + agent inspects frames **from the MP4** | `qc.txt`. Spec, black/frozen frames, loudness (−14 LUFS) |
| 10 | **Repair loop** | agent | fix → 7 → 8 → 9 until clean |
| 11 | **Export** | done | MP4 H.264/AAC, yuv420p, +faststart. **Publishing is not wired** (human review first) |

## Rules the agent must keep

- **Determinism:** every frame is a function of `t`. No `Math.random` (use `BM.hash`), no clocks, no network at render time.
- **Rigs:** joints use `BM.J`. GSAP never touches a joint's `transform`. The placement group and the animated group are separate elements.
- **Vertical (9:16) layout:** stack the story (screen above character, character above desk) instead of side by side. Keep camera zoom ≥ 1.05.
- **Sound:** every visible action that needs a sound gets a `BM.sfx` cue at the same `t`. Music sections are named styles.
- **Comments:** never put a `//` comment in the middle of a line of code. It silently disables the rest of the line (this broke two renders during testing).

## Integrations (prepared, not enabled)

- **ElevenLabs:** `tools/narration.py --provider elevenlabs --allow-paid`, plus `narration.allow_paid: true` in the brief, plus `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` in the environment.
- **Hermes / other agents:** write `brief.json`, then call `bin/bm-agent "<prompt>" --name X --run`, which runs headless Claude Code with a tool allowlist. Read `out/render-metrics.json` and `out/qc.txt`.
- **Instagram / TikTok:** deliver `out/<name>.mp4` (1080×1920, 30 fps, −14 LUFS). Auto-publishing is deliberately absent.
- **TOYA product ads:** start from `projects/aether-ad` (3D product + kinetic type). Swap the model for the real product (glTF) and the brand palette.
- **SlideSpoken explainers:** start from `projects/crypto-crash` (rig + expressions + stages). Bang Motion's explainer starters cover the 16:9 educational styles.

1	# Sarcastic Grotesque: face-first reaction-meme comedy
2	
3	`lib/grotesque.js` (`BM.GR`) is a **separate** character system: the simple `BM.CH` puppets are untouched. Use it when the brief asks for sarcastic, ugly-funny, meme-style or reaction comedy.
4	
5	The face is the punchline.
6	
7	- **Template:** `bin/bm-new <name> --dur 20 --template grotesque`
8	- **Sheets:** `library/grotesque/sheets/`
9	- **Style pack:** `BM.STYLE.use('grotesque')` (Anton meme subtitles)
10	
11	Load order:
12	
13	```html
14	<script src="../../vendor/gsap.min.js"></script>
15	<script src="../../lib/bm-core.js"></script>
16	<script src="../../lib/camera.js"></script>
17	<script src="../../lib/styles.js"></script>
18	<script src="../../lib/grotesque.js"></script>
19	```
20	
21	## The cast (original characters, fixed identities)
22	
23	Each character has a default attitude (their **base**), a distinct head silhouette, nose, teeth and voice.
24	
25	| id | who | look | base |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| `gary` | exhausted office employee | long droopy egg head, comb-over, eye bags, stubble, coffee-stained shirt | dead inside |
28	| `brock` | smug boss | wide boxy jaw, helmet hair, mustache, double chin, navy suit | smug |
29	| `kyle` | fake motivational manager | spray-tan, spiky blond quiff, headset, giant veneers, "TEAM LEAD" lanyard | fake smile |
30	| `vlad` | dramatic crypto trader | big potato head, bulging bloodshot eyes, mop and cowlick, gold ₿ chain, hoodie | panic |
31	| `tiff` | gossip girl | pointy heart-shaped chin, lashes, glossy lips, ponytail, hoops | side-eye |
32	| `bev` | judgmental auntie | jowly box head, curlers, red cat-eye glasses on a chain, chin mole, pearls | judgmental |
33	| `zeke` | weird influencer | split teal/pink mullet, ring-light eyes, crooked nose, tiny mustache, neon tank | psycho smile |
34	| `marco` | broke guy acting rich | long narrow face, slick hair, sunglasses on head, pencil mustache, gold tooth, chipped fake chain | overconfident |
35	| `dale` | overconfident salesman | huge shiny forehead dome, side tufts, cleft chin, horse teeth, plaid blazer | overconfident |
36	| `pip` | chaotic best friend | frizzy orange hair, buck teeth with a gap, freckles, band-aid, stripes | manic laugh |
37	
38	To build one, call `ch = GR.make(stageGroup, id, x, y, scale)`.
39	
40	- `(x, y)` is the **head centre**. The bust (shoulders and chest) hangs below, so put a desk or frame edge over the lower body.
41	- Scale 1 gives a head about 470 px tall.
42	
43	## Expressions (33): `GR.expr(ch, at, name)` morphs; `GR.react(ch, at, name, opts)` snaps
44	
45	Every expression actually reshapes the face: jaw length, eye size per eye, lid angles, mouth shape, crooked teeth, gums, tongue, wrinkles, folds and colour overlays. They aren't brow tweaks.
46	
47	The expressions, by group:
48	
49	- **Smug and sly:** smug, plotting, evilGrin, sarcasticClap, passiveAggro, overconfident, judgmental.
50	- **Fake:** fakeSmile, fakePro, psychoSmile.
51	- **Shock and fear:** shockScream, panic, terrified, whatDidISee, caughtLying, overwhelmed.
52	- **Negative:** disgust, cringe, jealous, suspicious, sideEye, embarrassed.
53	- **Broken:** deadInside, done, sleepyBroken.
54	- **Crying:** uglyCry, hystericalCry, heartbreak.
55	- **Rage:** angryMeltdown, unhingedRage.
56	- **Manic:** manicLaugh, greedy.
57	- **Reset:** neutral.
58	
59	Plain-English aliases also work, for example `'dead inside'`, `'caught lying'` or `'full unhinged rage'`.
60	
61	Some expressions bring hands automatically:
62	
63	| Expression | Hands |
64	|---|---|
65	| panic, terrified | hands on cheeks |
66	| angryMeltdown, unhingedRage | fists |
67	| plotting | steepled fingers |
68	| sarcasticClap | slow clap |
69	| greedy | rubbing hands |
70	| overwhelmed | grabbing head |
71	| embarrassed | scratching head |
72	| heartbreak | hand on chest |
73	| fakePro | adjusting tie |
74	| overconfident | thumbs up |
75	| caughtLying | shrug |
76	
77	Call `GR.hands(ch, at, preset)` to set them yourself. The presets are rest, cheeks, grabhead, facepalm, clap, fists, steeple, shrug, chest, rub, thumbs, point, scratch, tie, phone, selfie and temples.
78	
79	## Animation behaviour
80	
81	| Call | What it does |
82	|---|---|
83	| `GR.react(ch, at, name, {sc, shot, pop, sfx, smear, hands})` | **The reaction shot**: anticipation squash (0.12 s) → snap with overshoot → squash/stretch pulse, head jerk and smear ghosts → elastic settle. With `sc` it also punches the camera (`shot`: close, ecu or mouth). Default sfx is `boom` |
84	| `GR.pop(ch, at, hold)` | eyes pop out, pupils pinpoint |
85	| `GR.jawDrop(ch, at, amt, hold)` | jaw falls with a bounce and the skull stretches |
86	| `GR.blink`, `GR.jerk(ch, at, dx, dy)`, `GR.recoil` | exaggerated blink, head jerk, recoil |
87	| `GR.smear(ch, at)` | smear frames |
88	| `GR.tremble(ch, t0, t1, amp)`, `GR.wobble(ch, t0, t1)` | shaking, lip wobble |
89	| `GR.tearBurst(ch, t0, t1)` | tear fountains |
90	| `GR.hold(ch, t0, t1)` | **comedic hold**: stops idle drift and blinks, so the face freezes |
91	| `GR.laugh(ch, t0, t1)` | manic bouncing laugh |
92	| `GR.clap(ch, t0, t1, rate)` | slow sarcastic clap, synced to clap sfx |
93	| `GR.escalate(ch, t0, ['panic', 'terrified', 'hystericalCry', 'unhingedRage'], .55)` | rapid escalation, each step a snap |
94	| `GR.slide(ch, at, dx, dur)` | bust walks in or out with a bob |
95	| `GR.say(ch, t0, t1, text, {visemes})` | lip-synced talking on top of any expression, plus a meme subtitle |
96	
97	## Shot grammar (use it; it's what makes this style funny)
98	
99	1. **Framing** is set per character with `GR.frame(ch, kind)`, where kind is wide, medium, close, ecu (eyes) or mouth.
100	   - Hard cut: `GR.cutTo(sc, at, ch, kind)`.
101	   - Snap zoom with whoosh: `GR.punch(sc, at, ch, kind)`.
102	   - Creep-in on a hold: `GR.drift(sc, t0, dur)`.
103	2. **The beat:**
104	   1. **SETUP** in medium (1–2 s, a normal moment).
105	   2. **TRIGGER** (something happens; sfx).
106	   3. **SNAP REACTION:** `GR.react` with a punch to close or ecu, plus `GR.backdrop(ch, at, dur, 'speed'|'burst'|'rage'|'dread')`.
107	   4. **COMEDIC HOLD** of 0.6–1.2 s (`GR.hold`).
108	   5. **Hard cut** to the next beat.
109	3. **Coverage:**
110	   - At least 50 % of screen time is close-ups or ECUs.
111	   - Cut every 1.2–2.5 s.
112	   - No wide shot lasts more than 2 s.
113	   - Every video has at least three snap reactions.
114	4. **Contrast normal and absurd.** Stay calm and quiet right before the face explodes. Silence or crickets work before the boom.
115	5. **The punchline is a face.** End on an ECU reaction plus a meme caption (`GR.meme(at, dur, 'TEXT', {pos: 'top'})`) and a comedic sound (boom, rimshot, cricket, trombone, wrong, dun).
116	6. **Escalation.** Repeat the gag with bigger faces each time (rule of three), or use `GR.escalate`.
117	
118	## Sets and props
119	
120	- **Sets:** `GR.BG.office(p)`, `GR.BG.desk(p, x, y)`.
121	- **Reaction backgrounds:** `GR.BG.burst`, `.speed`, `.dread`, `.rage`, `.void`.

# Sarcastic Grotesque: face-first reaction-meme comedy

`lib/grotesque.js` (`BM.GR`) is a **separate** character system: the simple `BM.CH` puppets are untouched. Use it when the brief asks for sarcastic, ugly-funny, meme-style or reaction comedy.

The face is the punchline.

- **Template:** `bin/bm-new <name> --dur 20 --template grotesque`
- **Sheets:** `library/grotesque/sheets/`
- **Style pack:** `BM.STYLE.use('grotesque')` (Anton meme subtitles)

Load order:

```html
<script src="../../vendor/gsap.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../lib/bm-core.js"></script>
<script src="../../lib/camera.js"></script>
<script src="../../lib/styles.js"></script>
<script src="../../lib/grotesque.js"></script>
```

## The cast (original characters, fixed identities)

Each character has a default attitude (their **base**), a distinct head silhouette, nose, teeth and voice.

| id | who | look | base |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gary` | exhausted office employee | long droopy egg head, comb-over, eye bags, stubble, coffee-stained shirt | dead inside |
| `brock` | smug boss | wide boxy jaw, helmet hair, mustache, double chin, navy suit | smug |
| `kyle` | fake motivational manager | spray-tan, spiky blond quiff, headset, giant veneers, "TEAM LEAD" lanyard | fake smile |
| `vlad` | dramatic crypto trader | big potato head, bulging bloodshot eyes, mop and cowlick, gold ₿ chain, hoodie | panic |
| `tiff` | gossip girl | pointy heart-shaped chin, lashes, glossy lips, ponytail, hoops | side-eye |
| `bev` | judgmental auntie | jowly box head, curlers, red cat-eye glasses on a chain, chin mole, pearls | judgmental |
| `zeke` | weird influencer | split teal/pink mullet, ring-light eyes, crooked nose, tiny mustache, neon tank | psycho smile |
| `marco` | broke guy acting rich | long narrow face, slick hair, sunglasses on head, pencil mustache, gold tooth, chipped fake chain | overconfident |
| `dale` | overconfident salesman | huge shiny forehead dome, side tufts, cleft chin, horse teeth, plaid blazer | overconfident |
| `pip` | chaotic best friend | frizzy orange hair, buck teeth with a gap, freckles, band-aid, stripes | manic laugh |

To build one, call `ch = GR.make(stageGroup, id, x, y, scale)`.

- `(x, y)` is the **head centre**. The bust (shoulders and chest) hangs below, so put a desk or frame edge over the lower body.
- Scale 1 gives a head about 470 px tall.

## Expressions (33): `GR.expr(ch, at, name)` morphs; `GR.react(ch, at, name, opts)` snaps

Every expression actually reshapes the face: jaw length, eye size per eye, lid angles, mouth shape, crooked teeth, gums, tongue, wrinkles, folds and colour overlays. They aren't brow tweaks.

The expressions, by group:

- **Smug and sly:** smug, plotting, evilGrin, sarcasticClap, passiveAggro, overconfident, judgmental.
- **Fake:** fakeSmile, fakePro, psychoSmile.
- **Shock and fear:** shockScream, panic, terrified, whatDidISee, caughtLying, overwhelmed.
- **Negative:** disgust, cringe, jealous, suspicious, sideEye, embarrassed.
- **Broken:** deadInside, done, sleepyBroken.
- **Crying:** uglyCry, hystericalCry, heartbreak.
- **Rage:** angryMeltdown, unhingedRage.
- **Manic:** manicLaugh, greedy.
- **Reset:** neutral.

Plain-English aliases also work, for example `'dead inside'`, `'caught lying'` or `'full unhinged rage'`.

Some expressions bring hands automatically:

| Expression | Hands |
|---|---|
| panic, terrified | hands on cheeks |
| angryMeltdown, unhingedRage | fists |
| plotting | steepled fingers |
| sarcasticClap | slow clap |
| greedy | rubbing hands |
| overwhelmed | grabbing head |
| embarrassed | scratching head |
| heartbreak | hand on chest |
| fakePro | adjusting tie |
| overconfident | thumbs up |
| caughtLying | shrug |

Call `GR.hands(ch, at, preset)` to set them yourself. The presets are rest, cheeks, grabhead, facepalm, clap, fists, steeple, shrug, chest, rub, thumbs, point, scratch, tie, phone, selfie and temples.

## Animation behaviour

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GR.react(ch, at, name, {sc, shot, pop, sfx, smear, hands})` | **The reaction shot**: anticipation squash (0.12 s) → snap with overshoot → squash/stretch pulse, head jerk and smear ghosts → elastic settle. With `sc` it also punches the camera (`shot`: close, ecu or mouth). Default sfx is `boom` |
| `GR.pop(ch, at, hold)` | eyes pop out, pupils pinpoint |
| `GR.jawDrop(ch, at, amt, hold)` | jaw falls with a bounce and the skull stretches |
| `GR.blink`, `GR.jerk(ch, at, dx, dy)`, `GR.recoil` | exaggerated blink, head jerk, recoil |
| `GR.smear(ch, at)` | smear frames |
| `GR.tremble(ch, t0, t1, amp)`, `GR.wobble(ch, t0, t1)` | shaking, lip wobble |
| `GR.tearBurst(ch, t0, t1)` | tear fountains |
| `GR.hold(ch, t0, t1)` | **comedic hold**: stops idle drift and blinks, so the face freezes |
| `GR.laugh(ch, t0, t1)` | manic bouncing laugh |
| `GR.clap(ch, t0, t1, rate)` | slow sarcastic clap, synced to clap sfx |
| `GR.escalate(ch, t0, ['panic', 'terrified', 'hystericalCry', 'unhingedRage'], .55)` | rapid escalation, each step a snap |
| `GR.slide(ch, at, dx, dur)` | bust walks in or out with a bob |
| `GR.say(ch, t0, t1, text, {visemes})` | lip-synced talking on top of any expression, plus a meme subtitle |

## Shot grammar (use it; it's what makes this style funny)

1. **Framing** is set per character with `GR.frame(ch, kind)`, where kind is wide, medium, close, ecu (eyes) or mouth.
   - Hard cut: `GR.cutTo(sc, at, ch, kind)`.
   - Snap zoom with whoosh: `GR.punch(sc, at, ch, kind)`.
   - Creep-in on a hold: `GR.drift(sc, t0, dur)`.
2. **The beat:**
   1. **SETUP** in medium (1–2 s, a normal moment).
   2. **TRIGGER** (something happens; sfx).
   3. **SNAP REACTION:** `GR.react` with a punch to close or ecu, plus `GR.backdrop(ch, at, dur, 'speed'|'burst'|'rage'|'dread')`.
   4. **COMEDIC HOLD** of 0.6–1.2 s (`GR.hold`).
   5. **Hard cut** to the next beat.
3. **Coverage:**
   - At least 50 % of screen time is close-ups or ECUs.
   - Cut every 1.2–2.5 s.
   - No wide shot lasts more than 2 s.
   - Every video has at least three snap reactions.
4. **Contrast normal and absurd.** Stay calm and quiet right before the face explodes. Silence or crickets work before the boom.
5. **The punchline is a face.** End on an ECU reaction plus a meme caption (`GR.meme(at, dur, 'TEXT', {pos: 'top'})`) and a comedic sound (boom, rimshot, cricket, trombone, wrong, dun).
6. **Escalation.** Repeat the gag with bigger faces each time (rule of three), or use `GR.escalate`.

## Sets and props

- **Sets:** `GR.BG.office(p)`, `GR.BG.desk(p, x, y)`.
- **Reaction backgrounds:** `GR.BG.burst`, `.speed`, `.dread`, `.rage`, `.void`.
- **Monitor:** `m = GR.monitor(p, x, y, s, {key: GR.SCREENS.meme|spreadsheet|crash|off})`. Switch screens with `m.flip(at, key)`.
- **Captions:** `GR.meme(at, dur, text)` for top/bottom meme text; `GR.label(at, dur, '9:01 AM')`.
- **Other places:** build any other set with plain SVG (`BM.R`, `BM.PA`) using **thick ink outlines (#16110E, stroke 7–9) and muted, dirty colours**. Draw the set behind the characters, and any foreground (desk, car door, phone frame) after them.

## Sound

- **Comedy sfx:**
  - impacts and cues: boom, zoom_in, punch, dun, wrong, gong;
  - camera and face moves: whoosh, slide_down, slide_up, eyepop;
  - comedy reactions: rimshot, cricket, trombone, gasp, laugh, squish;
  - hands and objects: clap, keys, notify, register.
- **Music:** awkward, drama, sneaky, tension, hype, sad.
- **Mix:** keep the music low (gain 0.5–0.7). The face sfx carry the jokes.

## Quality gate (check before accepting a render; iterate if any answer is "no")

1. Is every reaction readable at phone size within 0.5 s, from the face alone?
2. Do the faces actually deform (jaw, eyes, mouth shape), or did only the brows move?
3. Are at least half the frames close-ups or ECUs, with at least three snap reactions?
4. Is there a calm "normal" beat before each absurd face?
5. Does the video end on a face punchline with a held frame of at least 1 s?
6. Is there nothing cute or plain on screen: every character in a strong attitude, never idle-neutral for long?
